<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

chainglass reads the pij fleet by shelling out `pij list --json --badge` on an 8s loop. That call grew from ~0.7s at 181 rows (measured when it was written, pij-records.ts:127) to 7.744s at ~1,200 rows, while PijRecords caps every call at PIJ_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000. Every call is therefore killed before it returns: the loop paid ~95% of a core continuously and received nothing. The loop is now off (03695dd68); the rail is dark either way.

pij-rs answers the same question over HTTP in 113ms for 598 seats, and offers an event stream that removes polling entirely. This plan builds that reader behind a PIJ_SOURCE flag defaulting to legacy. It does NOT flip the default: that is gated on work owned by the pij-rs team (plan-129 fleet migration, req-0040 role writer) and on acceptance evidence gathered against a live daemon.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Read the pij fleet over HTTP from pij-rs instead of spawning a process per tick.
- Replace polling with a single /v1/events subscriber carrying a cursor, surviving reconnect and key rotation.
- Keep the existing IPijRecords seam so the poller, routes and UI are unchanged.
- Render fields pij-rs does not carry as explicitly unavailable, never blank and never synthesised.
- Leave the switch flippable in one env var the day the fleet migration lands.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Flipping the default to rs. Gated on plan-129 and req-0040, both owned by the pij-rs team.
- Any write path. chainglass is a reader: no register, send, adopt or close from the UI.
- Reading ~/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite directly. The HTTP surface is the contract.
- Restoring the legacy path's performance. It is being deleted, not repaired.
- Reconciling seat identity across the two daemons. chainglass renders what rs reports.

<a id="risks-assumptions"></a>

## Risks & Assumptions

ASSUMPTION, load-bearing: pij-rs is the fleet's future and the legacy daemon is being retired today. If that reverses, this plan is wasted work and the legacy path needs repair instead.

RISK: the flip is gated on two items this repo does not own. plan-129 migrates the fleet into the rs roster (24 of 28 live seats are absent from it today); req-0040 adds a role writer (role is null on all 598 rs seats, so primes and PMs cross over unroled). Until both land, flipping renders a rail that is emptier and less governed than the one it replaces.

RISK, discovered while planning: seat IDENTITY is not preserved across the daemons. One process (pid 69672, proc_start 20260824102712) is pij-chief-roadrunner in legacy and pij-lonely-antelope in rs. rs adopts INTO the row that already owns a pane (identity.rs:466-480), so a pre-claimed pane silently inherits the older id. Across the 28 live legacy seats: 1 same id, 3 renamed, 24 absent. chainglass cannot fix this and must not try — it renders what rs reports. Recorded because the rail will show unfamiliar names and that will look like a chainglass bug.

CONSEQUENCE for verification: 'match the legacy reader for the same seat' is NOT a constructible proof for most of the fleet, because the two daemons disagree about which seat a process is. The acceptance criteria therefore measure against the LIVE rs daemon and against fleet behaviour (appear/disappear within 2s), never against legacy output.
